title: Reconstructing and Understanding Pre‐GRACE Terrestrial Water Storage Changes in a Large Himalayan River Basin via Dual‐Constraint Hydrological Calibration
content:
Abstract

This study develops a dual-constraint calibration framework combining streamflow observations and GRACE-derived terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) to reconstruct long-term storage changes in the Yarlung Tsangpo-Brahmaputra River Basin (YBRB). Three VIC calibration schemes were evaluated: grid-scale dual calibration (TQ_GRID), subbasin-scale dual calibration (TQ_SUB), and subbasin-scale streamflow-only calibration (Q_SUB). Both dual-calibration schemes improved TWSA simulation relative to Q_SUB, but TQ_SUB provided the best balance between discharge performance, TWSA agreement, and physical coherence, achieving a basin-scale TWSA NSE of 0.88 compared with 0.78 for Q_SUB and 0.83 for TQ_GRID. Using TQ_SUB, we reconstructed monthly TWSA during 1965–2015. Reconstructed basin-scale TWSA declined significantly at −5.87 mm yr−1, with stronger loss after 2005 (−7.58 mm yr−1), and the Tibetan Plateau region showed the strongest decline (−8.05 mm yr−1). Component attribution indicates that glacier water storage dominated the long-term trend, while soil moisture storage controlled seasonal variability and jointly influenced interannual anomalies with glacier water storage and snow water equivalent. This study provides a dual-constraint calibration framework for extending satellite-era storage information into long-term hydrological reconstruction, offering process-based insights into water-storage dynamics in large high-mountain transboundary basins.
